title: Verb constructions 2
subtitle: advise me to go, warn me that, remind me to
summary: Use reporting verbs such as advise, persuade, warn, remind and encourage with the right construction after them.

lesson.heading: A great opportunity
lesson.text: Read what a young photographer says about a job offer in Italy. Notice the verb after each person's reaction.

examples.text: My best friend thought it was a fantastic opportunity and **advised me to go**.
Dad didn't try to **persuade me not to go**, but he **warned me that** it would be hard work.
He **reminded me that** it was only three months, then I'd be out of a job.
I **realised that** my girlfriend wasn't happy about it either.
I **promised her that** I would phone every day.
I **suggested that** she could come out to Italy for a holiday.
I didn't **mention that** I was part of a small team.

lesson.heading: The verbs and their constructions
rows: say what you think someone should do
make someone agree to do something by talking a lot
tell someone that something bad may happen
tell someone something so that they don't forget it
understand something you didn't understand before
say you will certainly do something
tell someone about a possible idea or plan
say something, often briefly or quickly
lesson.note: Some of these verbs take more than one construction: I suggested going there. She warned me not to go. He reminded me to post the letter.

lesson.heading: Verb + (that) ...
lesson.text: These verbs are followed by a clause with or without **that**: **say**, **hope**, **notice**, **recommend** and **expect**.

examples.text: I **said that** I was busy.
I **hope (that)** you'll come and see us soon.
When I left, I **noticed that** the door was open.
I **recommended that** we all go together, so no one gets lost.
I **expect (that)** he'll ring us later.
examples.note: expect = think or believe something will happen

lesson.heading: Verb + object + (that) ...
lesson.text: After **tell**, **show** and **convince** you must name the person before the clause.

examples.text: I **told them (that)** they could leave early.
He tried to **convince me that** I needed some new clothes.

lesson.heading: Verb + object + to infinitive
lesson.text: These verbs need a person and then **to** + infinitive: **ask**, **tell**, **want**, **allow**, **expect**, **remind**, **help** and **encourage**.

examples.text: Tracey **asked me to look** after her cat.
They **told us to wait** outside.
They **want us to stay** at school.
I had to **remind him to buy** the food.
She **helped me to write** the report.
examples.note: You can also say: She helped me write the report.

examples.text: My parents **encouraged me to read**.

lesson.text: Say does not take a person: I said the film was terrible, but I told her the film was terrible.

exercises.prompt: She encouraged me ___ for the job.
exercises.explanation: Encourage takes an object and then a to infinitive.
Allow takes an object and then a to infinitive: allowed us to go.

exercises.statement: He said me the film was terrible.
exercises.explanation: He said the film was terrible. Say does not take a person; use tell for that: He told me the film was terrible.
Advise takes an object and then a to infinitive.

exercises.prompt: He reminded me ___ to the bank before it closed.
exercises.explanation: Remind + object + to infinitive: he reminded me to go.
Want takes an object and a to infinitive, never a that clause.

exercises.prompt: The path was dangerous, so I warned them ___ there alone.
Match each verb with its meaning.

pairs.right: make someone agree by talking a lot
say that something bad may happen

exercises.prompt: When we went in, I ___ that people were looking at us.
exercises.explanation: Notice means you could see something. It is followed by a that clause.

exercises.prompt: I didn't want the job, but my mother ___ me to take it.
exercises.explanation: Persuade + object + to infinitive: persuaded me to take it.

exercises.prompt: I wasn't sure about the plan, but my boss ___ me that it would work.
exercises.explanation: Convince + object + (that) ... means make someone believe something.

exercises.prompt: Fortunately Aidan ___ me that it was Marsha's birthday; I'd forgotten.
exercises.explanation: Remind + object + (that) ... means tell someone so they do not forget.

exercises.prompt: Which construction does each verb take?

exercises.answer: She helped me to write the report
exercises.explanation: Help takes an object and then to + infinitive. You can also leave out to: She helped me write the report.
